summary.headline: H2 FY26 revenue fell to Rs 28.97 crore with 5.32% EBITDA margin as management deferred loss-making fixed-price contracts amid component inflation.
summary.overview: Takyon reported H2 FY26 (Oct 2025 to Mar 2026) consolidated revenue of Rs 28.97 crore, EBITDA of Rs 1.61 crore (5.32% margin) and PAT of Rs 0.44 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue was Rs 71.05 crore, EBITDA Rs 7.09 crore (near 10%), PAT Rs 3.65 crore and EPS Rs 3.29. H1 FY26 revenue was Rs 42.08 crore with EBITDA margin near 13%. Management attributed the H2 shortfall to component price inflation and lengthened lead times, and said it chose to defer unviable fixed-price contracts and protect the balance sheet. Total liabilities fell from Rs 50 crore to Rs 12.20 crore and trade payables from Rs 30.21 crore to Rs 3.77 crore.

financial_highlights.change: c.31% lower than FY25 per analyst question; not disputed by management
down from Rs 50 crore, c.75% reduction
management says lowest in peer group

segments.name: Supply and installation (fixed-price, largely)
segments.commentary: Of the Rs 32 crore confirmed order book, about Rs 20 crore is supply and installation, largely fixed-price from last year; OEM prices are reportedly frozen for these contracts. Management says escalated prices were built into bidding for new contracts.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: About Rs 12 crore of the order book is operation and maintenance services, contracted quarterly.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to be meaningfully higher than FY26; management says it will surpass FY24-FY25 levels by close to 15% (also referenced 15-20% growth on a Rs 100 crore baseline) and called FY26's Rs 71 crore not a new base.
H1 FY27 target: chasing at least a repeat of H1 FY26 revenue of Rs 42 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at around 11-13% for the full year; management declined to forecast H1 margin given expected turbulence for the next 3-4 months.
Of the Rs 32 crore order book, Rs 27-28 crore expected to be billed; Rs 20-22 crore expected to be billed in H1 FY27; Rs 4-5 crore of multi-year revenue to spill over 2-3 years.
Management said no point-specific revenue guidance is provided.
Target customer mix in 2-3 years: 30% state governments, 40% PSUs, 30% enterprise (currently 85% government, 15% enterprise; government split c.60% state / 40% PSU).
capex_capacity: Confirmed executable order book of Rs 32 crore as on 31 March 2026, with fresh orders of Rs 3.2 crore received in the following 45 days.
Average project cycle of 4 to 5 months from bidding through procurement, supply and payment.

Supply lead times for certain critical IT hardware stretched from 8-12 weeks to 9-52 weeks; management said vendors were giving only 30-day price validity and the company declined to bid such projects.
Management expects component turbulence to last 3-4 more months per OEM and industry feedback.
Geographic expansion: senior technical-commercial hire in Mumbai for BFSI customers; continued focus on North East (Assam, Tripura and other seven sister states).
demand_pricing: Component prices for switches, firewalls, compute and storage rose 40% to over 300% in some items, per management, attributed to AI data-centre demand absorbing global manufacturing capacity.
Management says no customers or market share were lost in H2; one Rs 5 crore services contract ended and was re-entered into the bidding process, with re-entry expected in June.
Company is pursuing BFSI (previously minimal in book) and DPDP Act compliance awareness with existing customers; no DPDP order book visibility yet.
Mitigation: diversified vendors, added price escalation clauses to new contracts, locked better supplier visibility, and shifted procurement toward Make in India product lines.

Management cited peers Allied Digital (standalone swung from Rs 10 crore profit to net loss in FY26) and Tejas Networks (revenue down 82% in Q4 FY26) as evidence of margin damage from chasing revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and any FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book Rs 32 crore as of 31 March 2026, with Rs 3.2 crore new orders in the following 45 days; no point revenue guidance, but FY27 expected meaningfully above FY26 and about 15% above FY24-FY25 levels.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is fixed price?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 20 crore supply and installation (largely fixed-price) and Rs 12 crore quarterly O&M services; management says OEMs have frozen prices on current fixed-price orders, so no further escalation in the existing book.

qa_highlights.question: Was the H2 shortfall supply chain or execution-related?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no execution failures, project cancellations or quantitative losses; the shortfall was due to price inflation and supply disruption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the government vs non-government mix and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 85% government and 15% enterprise, with government split about 60% state and 40% PSU; target in 2-3 years is 30% state, 40% PSU, 30% enterprise.

qa_highlights.question: Why will supply constraints normalise in 3-4 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this reflects OEM and industry feedback that current orders now carry firm timelines of 3-4 months; it said the company had not forecast a 3-4 month normalisation as a fixed number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 full-year EBITDA margin to 11-13%, having delivered close to 10% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 revenue a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, FY26 is not a baseline; it was driven by geopolitical and supply-chain disruption, and it sees 15-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Any lost orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a contract ended and was re-bid on fresh procurement rather than being lost; one Rs 5 crore order was cancelled with re-entry expected in June.

risks_watch: Component price inflation and vendor price validity (30 days) could further pressure margins on new orders and limit bid participation.
Management's 3-4 month normalisation timeline is industry-based and not confirmed; analyst challenged it as possibly optimistic.

Revenue visibility: Rs 20-22 crore of the Rs 32 crore book billable in H1 FY27, and the FY27 growth target relies on pipeline conversion that management could not quantify; DPDP and BFSI order flow are unproven.
Working capital: management acknowledged the government-heavy mix lengthens the working capital cycle.
Management said the Rs 5 crore re-entry is expected in June; watch whether it is re-won.

Full-year numbers reported on a consolidated basis; several figures were stated imprecisely on the call (for example the Rs 100 crore baseline and the 15% vs 15-20% growth references), so reconcile against the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet and long-term strategy, but cautious and sometimes evasive on forward numbers: management declined point revenue guidance and gave ranges and qualitative targets. It was emphatic that there were no execution failures and that the H2 shortfall was a deliberate choice to avoid loss-making fixed-price contracts.
key_quotes: We had two choices, execute at a loss to protect the headline revenues, or to protect the balance sheet. We choose financial discipline.
But in H2 Financial Year 26, That was materially impacted by an extraordinary, externally-driven global supply chain crisis.
So, one 5 crore order, we didn't lose it, but we, with the good relation with the customer, we managed to, get it, get the, get it canceled.
Our debt-to-equity ratio is lowest in our peer groups, which stands at just 0.12.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue about 15% above FY25 levels and a 11-13% EBITDA margin, backed by a Rs 32 crore confirmed order book (Rs 20-22 crore billable in H1 FY27) but no new capacity, with growth in the 15% range not separately quantified as a YoY percentage.
